question.text: Under SEBI (PM) Regulations 2020, derivatives in fixed-income PMS strategies are primarily used for:

answer.text: Hedging of portfolio risks and duration management

explanation.text: The Logic: Derivatives in PMS are permitted for hedging and portfolio rebalancing on terms set out in the Portfolio Management Agreement, subject to disclosure and permission requirements. In fixed-income portfolios, derivatives are used to hedge interest-rate / duration risk and manage duration gaps. The Trap: Unlimited speculation is not the regulatory intent. Arbitrage alone and collateral repledging do not describe the permitted use of derivatives in PMS fixed-income strategies. Note: The regulatory frame is hedging and portfolio rebalancing under the PMS agreement, with derivatives used in fixed income to manage interest-rate / duration risk.
